facts.says: The Grand Tree is a living tree with the gnomes' town built inside it, in the north-east of the Stronghold, and the gnomes call it Ta Quir Priw.
Inside the Grand Tree the king holds court on the ground floor, the shops, bar and banks are a floor up, Gulluck's weapon shop is above that, and the glider and a small jail are right at the top.
The Grand Tree shelters most of the gnomes living in Gielinor, so its health matters to the whole race.
The Grand Tree's roots run so far that they poke up out of the water in Grandroot Bay, north of the tree.
Hazelmere, an old gnome mage and advisor to King Healthorg, was one of those who first grew and tended the Grand Tree, and he never cared to speak the common tongue.
Anita, who lives up a ladder in the north-west corner of the Stronghold, wrote the book gnomes use to translate old Gnomish.
King Narnode Shareen rules the Tree Gnome Stronghold and receives visitors on the ground floor of the Grand Tree, greeting humans graciously.
Narnode sends gnome explorers out to map the far corners of Gielinor, such as Wingstone in the desert and Penwie on Karamja.
The gnomes keep ambassadors at human courts: Ferrnook with King Roald, Gimblewap with King Lathas, and Spanfipple at the White Knights' Castle.
Oaknock the Engineer built most of the Stronghold long ago, there are statues to him about the place, and gnomes rank him just below King Healthorg.
King Healthorg the Great led the gnomes up from underground to settle the Stronghold, and his statues stand by the Stronghold gate and by the southern ramp up to the Grand Tree.
Gnomes were the ones who brought orange trees to Gielinor.
Gnomes stand two or three feet tall, have pointed ears, rarely grow beards, and mostly wear green with red or green pointed hats.
Gnomes are peaceable at heart, but years of trouble from goblins and humans mean most of them, ordinary folk included, carry a bow.
Gnomes hold to Guthix, the god of balance; their children say prayers to him and grown gnomes cry 'Great Guthix!' when surprised.
Brimstail, one of the few gnomes who practises magic, lives in a little cave by the river in the south-west of the Stronghold and can send folk to the essence mine.
Arposandra is said to be a gnome city founded long ago by the exile Glouphrie, but nobody knows where it is and some doubt it exists at all.
Gnome gliders fly from the top of the Grand Tree to White Wolf Mountain, Al Kharid, Karamja and the Feldip Hills, and pilots call each stop by its Gnomish name.
Captain Errdo flies the glider from the top of the Grand Tree, Captain Dalbur the one at Al Kharid, Captain Bleemadge the one on White Wolf Mountain and Captain Klemfoodle the one on Karamja.
The glider route to Lemanto Andra, by the Digsite, only goes one way, because the glider crashes on landing every time.
Oaknock used to make little model gliders for his children, and his son Yewnock grew up to build the real gnome glider from them.
A spirit tree, one of the ancient trees that can think and send travellers to other spirit trees, stands in the middle of the Stronghold just south of the Grand Tree.
There's a landing spot for hot air balloons just south of the Grand Tree, with routes to places like Entrana, Taverley and Varrock.
Assistant Le Smith works the Grand Tree balloon for Auguste; he used to be a glider pilot until he was thrown out for being too full of hot air.
Gnomeball is played on a field in the north-west of the Stronghold: grab the ball from the referee, dodge or pass to the green wingers, and throw it through the net, with five goals to win.
Gnomeball has very few rules and lots of tackling; the referee admits humans have died on the field, there's blood on the pitch, and leaving with no broken limbs counts as doing well.
The agility course just south of the Grand Tree runs over a log, up nets and branches, along a tightrope and through pipes, and it's the gentlest course there is: nobody falls off it.
The gnome trainers on the agility course shout at everyone like drill sergeants, telling slow runners their granny moves faster.
Blurberry runs the cocktail bar a floor up in the Grand Tree, and there's a second Blurberry Bar east of the gnomeball field.
Gnome cocktails include the fruit blast, pineapple punch, wizard blizzard, short green guy, drunk dragon, chocolate saturday and the Blurberry special.
Heckel Funch sells cocktail makings in the Grand Tree, from vodka, gin and whisky to lemons, limes, oranges and pineapples.
Gnome cooking runs to crunchies, battas and gnomebowls: toad crunchies, worm battas, worm holes, vegetable balls, chocolate bombs and tangled toad's legs.
Hudo keeps the grocery in the Grand Tree, selling Gianne dough and gnome cooking ingredients, and he'll pay well for giant frog legs.
The swamp in the north-west of the Stronghold is where gnomes catch toads for their legs and dig king worms for the kitchen.
Rometti, a very well-dressed gnome, sells gnome robes, hats and boots in pink, green, blue, cream and turquoise in the Grand Tree, all cut to fit humans.
Gnomes train giant battle tortoises in a pen north-west of the Grand Tree, each ridden by a driver, an archer and a mage, under Trainer Nacklepen.
Gnomes ride terrorbirds, big flightless birds kept in an enclosure on the west side of the Stronghold.
Nieve, a fearsome human slayer master, stands by the Stronghold Slayer Cave near the south bank, handing out monster-hunting tasks only to the toughest fighters.
The Grand Tree is sick and its roots are dying, and nobody in the Stronghold knows why.
King Narnode is worried sick about the Grand Tree and is asking passing travellers for help finding out what's wrong with it.
Gnomes argue over whether the Grand Tree's sickness is human sabotage or something closer to home.
Glough, the head tree guardian, lives in a treehouse just south-east of the ramp up to the Grand Tree and makes no secret that he doesn't trust humans.
It was Glough poisoning the Grand Tree all along, with daconia rocks, the one thing made to be able to kill it, which he had a hired human fetch from Hazelmere using a forged royal seal.
Glough meant to turn the dead Grand Tree's wood into warships, and had a shipyard on Karamja building a fleet to invade the human kingdoms.
When the human looking into the tree got too close, Glough set a black demon on them in the tunnels under the Grand Tree, and the human killed it.
Narnode had believed Glough and begun readying for war with the humans, but once the truth came out he apologised and called it off.
Narnode forced Glough to resign and keeps him under house arrest in his treehouse.
Daero is the new head tree guardian, usually found by Blurberry's bar, and unlike Glough he's friendly towards humans.
Since the last daconia rock was dug out from its roots, the Grand Tree has been fine, and the human who saved it may now fly the gliders and use the mine under the tree.
Narnode sent the 10th Squad, elite soldiers of his Royal Guard, to shut down Glough's old shipyard on Karamja, and nothing has been heard from them since.
Strong winds blew the 10th Squad's military gliders off course onto Crash Island, and most of them were taken prisoner by the monkeys of Ape Atoll next door.
King Awowogei of the monkeys had been secretly plotting with Glough's followers, and they sent a jungle demon to wipe out the 10th Squad.
The human who found the 10th Squad got about Ape Atoll disguised as a monkey, using a charm made by Zooknock, the squad's mage.
Sergeant Garkor made the human an honorary member of the 10th Squad, and together they killed the jungle demon, after which Daero gave the human combat training.
Glough has vanished from house arrest, and King Narnode wants the human who stopped him before to track him down.
Since Glough disappeared, the king wants his treehouse south-east of the Grand Tree searched for any clue to where he went.
Anita is Glough's sweetheart, though they keep separate houses.
It was Assistant Le Smith, the balloon man, who smuggled Glough out of house arrest and flew him to Ape Atoll.
On Ape Atoll Glough had been dosing monkeys and gorillas with a brew of his own, breeding savage gorillas he meant to control.
Glough's airship came over the Stronghold and loosed tortured gorillas into its north-west corner, and they were fought off by the 10th Squad, Nieve and a human.
Glough's airship crashed just north of the Stronghold, killing Le Smith; the wreck still lies there, and demonic gorillas lurk in the cavern beneath it.
In the cavern under the crash Glough drank his own brew and turned into a monster, was beaten, and the cave came down on him.
Nieve charged the mutated Glough, was flung against the cavern wall and killed by a falling boulder, and her gravestone stands between the swamp and the Grand Tree's north-west door.
Nieve's younger cousin Steve has taken over her post as the slayer master by the Stronghold Slayer Cave.
King Awowogei came to the Stronghold himself and made peace with King Narnode, and the gates of Marim on Ape Atoll are now open to all visitors.
Since the peace, a glider flies from the Grand Tree to Ape Atoll, which the pilots call Ookookolly Undri.
The 10th Squad are back in the Stronghold: Sergeant Garkor has moved into Glough's old treehouse, and Zooknock the squad mage lives up by the gnomeball field.
Anita has moved on from Glough and is now sweet on Carado, a soldier of the 10th Squad.
